title: Powerball winning ticket sold at Montvale, NJ Wegmans for $847 million jackpot
text:
Powerball winning ticket sold at Montvale, NJ Wegmans for $847 million jackpot - ABC7 New York 
 24/7 Live New York City New Jersey Long Island Northern Suburbs Connecticut PERSONAL FINANCE 
 One lucky New Jersey winner hits $847 million Powerball jackpot, ninth-largest ever awarded 
 Friday, November 6, 2026 12:10AM 
 Toni Yates has the details from Montvale, New Jersey. WABC NEW JERSEY (WABC) -- Someone in New Jersey woke up $847 million richer after a single ticket won the Powerball jackpot.
 The ticket was sold at a Wegmans Food Market in Montvale. The store was awarded a $30,000 bonus check on Thursday afternoon and officials there said they would donate the entire check to the Community Food Bank of New Jersey.
 "We are in the middle of our Check Out Hunger campaign, and we are going to donate the check directly to that campaign," said store manager Nick Tassi.
 The winning ticket matched all six numbers, making it the ninth-largest jackpot in Powerball history.
 Officials at the press conference Thursday said they did not know who the winner was yet and urged anyone who purchased a ticket to double check them.
 "My phone has been nonstop, and suddenly people are calling their friends seeing if they played the lottery," said Montvale Mayor Mike Ghassali.
 The lucky winner should sign the ticket immediately, make copies, and store it in a safe place prior to claiming their prize. The New Jersey Lottery recommends the winner meet with financial and legal advisors.
 Winners in New Jersey have one year from the date of the drawing to claim their prize.
 "This incredible prize marks another great record for New Jersey and proves just how lucky our players can be. We are excited to meet the winner soon," said New Jersey Lottery Executive Director James Carey.
 The winning numbers were 15, 34, 41, 53, and 56, with a Powerball of 21. The Power Play multiplier was 2.
 The winner can choose between the full $847 million jackpot paid out in annual installments over 29 years or a one-time cash payment of $363.1 million. Both amounts are before taxes.
 The win comes less than three months after a ticket sold in Illinois hit a $1.04 billion Powerball jackpot in August. The two prizes now rank as the eighth- and ninth-largest jackpots in Powerball history.
 The Powerball jackpot has reset to $20 million for Saturday's drawing.
 Prior to this, the Powerball jackpot was last won on August 12, when a single ticket sold in Illinois captured a $1.04 billion grand prize. There had been 35 consecutive drawings without a jackpot winner.
 This also marked the first jackpot cycle in which players in the United Kingdom have contributed to the prize pool from the start of the run, with every ticket sold contributing equally to jackpot growth.
 New Jersey's largest prize ever was a $1.13B Mega Millions prize on March 26, 2024.
